correctness.rationale: For any associative derivation D of M_n, innerness is established via matrix units. In odd characteristic, the image of an idempotent derivation is a square-zero two-sided ideal, hence zero by simplicity. In characteristic two, ad(A)^2=ad(A²) and idempotence is equivalent to A²+A scalar. Separability of this quadratic gives the split/irreducible dichotomy and the precise single rank law. If two idempotent inner derivations commute, their implementer commutator is scalar and lies in im(D)∩ker(D), so vanishes. Counting implementing matrices in each centralizer and dividing by q scalar shifts yields H and K; split and irreducible ranks are computed by eigenblock dimensions (for nonsplit, both field embeddings are used). The full coefficient-by-coefficient formula was independently checked by enumeration of normalized implementers over F2,F3,F4 at dimensions 2,3,4 as recorded in verify.py and verification_output.txt; finite checks are evidence, not the general proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed theorem is the complete ordered labeled bivariate rank polynomial for every finite full matrix algebra; it is distinct from grading-isomorphism classifications, isolated rank spectra or quadratic complex commutator resonance. The complete 2001 Caenepeel–Dăscălescu–Năstăsescu matrix-grading descent classification and 2020 Diniz–Pellegrino isomorphism-class counts are strong prior frameworks, explicitly credited, but their inspected theorems do not state the labeled simultaneous finite-field rank distribution. A closest complete source (Khazal/Boboc/Dascal̆escu) classifies M2 grading types including characteristic-two Klein-four cases but supplies no all-n finite-field pair/rank census. The complete matrix-ring derivation preprint by Ayupov/Arzikulov supplies structural background, not these multiplicities. published-finding corpus queries for aliases, quadratic centralizers, joint ranks and (C2)^2 gradings returned no implication covering the theorem. Historical priority remains provisional because more general grading enumeration may indirectly imply the formula.
residual_risks: A general finite-field Klein-four grading enumeration, if it already explicitly tabulates labeled simultaneous degrees, might imply the bivariate formula; not all such literature can be exhaustively checked.
The recent Diniz et al. full text was inaccessible; its explicit cyclic-subgroup hypothesis makes direct coverage unlikely but no whole-document negative claim is made.
Same-model proof and small finite checks are not an independent expert verification.

The full finite-abelian grading theory of Caenepeel et al. plus orbit-stabilizer computations might be developed elsewhere into the present joint rank formula; no all-literature priority proof is claimed.

value.rationale: The bivariate polynomial is a natural complete joint rank distribution for ordered commuting projection derivations (equivalently Klein-four grading eigenspaces in characteristic two), not a routine independent product of single-rank counts. Conditional fibers change sharply between split projections and irreducible Artin-Schreier quadratic implementers, and the nonsplit centralizer over F_{q²} has a distinct rank law. The formula covers every n and q and gives an explicit quantitative refinement of grading-isomorphism classifications. Small cases n=2,3,4 are illustrative, while its arbitrary-n exactness supplies future algebraic and probabilistic applications.
